answer:
Viterbi stores the best score ending in each state and a backpointer to its predecessor. At every timestep maximize previous_score+transition over predecessor states, then add the emission score. Trace backward from the final best state. Log space handles tiny probabilities, while −infinity marks impossible transitions. A CRF can reuse the recurrence with unnormalized scores; it may additionally require start/end potentials.

**Mathematical and practical explanation.** The recurrence is $\delta_t(j)=\log p(x_t|j)+\max_i[\delta_{t-1}(i)+\log p(j|i)]$. Store the maximizing predecessor for each state/time, then backtrack. Complexity is $O(TK^2)$ for K states with dense transitions; sparse transition structure can reduce work. Viterbi returns the most likely entire path, not independent marginal best states. [3](https://probml.github.io/pml-book/book1.html)

For the implementation or system context discussed above, see [1](https://spotintelligence.com/2025/06/02/viterbi-algorithm-made-simple-how-to-worked-out-examples/) and [2](https://web.stanford.edu/~jurafsky/slp3/A.pdf).
